name: Kelal
title: One Who Took a Foreign Wife in Exile
summary: Kelal was one of the Israelites from the family of Pahath-Moab who had taken a foreign (non-Jewish) wife during the period following the return from the Babylonian exile. He is mentioned in the book of Ezra as one of those who committed to sending away their foreign wives as part of Ezra's religious reforms to preserve the purity of the people.

keyEvents.title: Listed Among Those Who Took Foreign Wives
keyEvents.description: Kelal is mentioned among the men from the family of Pahath-Moab who had married foreign women, which was contrary to God's law.

keyEvents.title: Ezra's Call to Repentance
keyEvents.description: Ezra discovered that many Israelites, including Kelal, had taken foreign wives, and he urged the people to confess their sins to the Lord and separate themselves from the foreign women.

keyEvents.title: The People's Pledge to Send Away Foreign Wives
keyEvents.description: The whole assembly answered with a loud voice that they would do as Ezra said and send away their foreign wives and their children.

keyEvents.title: Investigative Commission Appointed
keyEvents.description: A commission was established to investigate all cases of marriage to foreign women, and the process was completed within three months.
